The autopsy report indicates that Ho Wai-ho had extensive burn injuries on his body, and soot deposits were found in his airway and lungs, showing that Ho was exposed to flames and thick smoke for a period of time before his death without wearing a breathing apparatus.

"Golden Suit" charred

The report pointed out that Ho's left-hand glove and hand hammer, breathing apparatus, axe, and gas detector were found respectively at the window edge on the 31st floor of Wang Tai House and in the lobby. His fire boots were found on the ground floor of Wang Tai House; photos show signs of melting on the boots. In addition, photos from the report show that Ho Wai-ho's "Golden Suit" was severely damaged at the left arm, and the left leg of his fire-resistant trousers was damaged with burn marks. According to records, the "Golden Suit" can withstand 1,093°C flames for 8 seconds.

168 deceased, female elderly account for 42%

In addition, the report also detailed the age and gender distribution of the 168 deceased. Among the 168 deceased, nearly 68% (114 people) were over 64 years old, of whom 71 were female and 43 were male. Six deceased were under 14 years old, all female; two deceased were aged 15 to 24, both female. Among the 79 injured, 25 suffered inhalation injuries, 22 had breathing difficulties, 3 had burns, and 2 suffered heat exhaustion, among other injuries.
